title: Acer Launches Predator Helios Gaming Laptops in India With RTX 5080 and Arrow Lake
excerpt: Three new models bring Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and Intel Arrow Lake processors to Indian gamers and creators, starting at Rs 2,42,990.
body:
• Acer launched three new Predator Helios gaming laptops in India featuring Nvidia RTX 50 Series GPUs and Intel Arrow Lake processors, with prices starting at Rs 2,42,990.
  • The flagship Predator Helios Neo 16 AI pairs an Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX processor with an RTX 5080 GPU and a 240Hz OLED display, targeting competitive gamers and content creators.
  • Acer India says coders and developers are driving demand for GPU-powered laptops, with EMI financing making high-end machines more accessible.
  • The laptops are available immediately at Acer stores, Amazon, Flipkart, Croma, Reliance, and Vijay Sales, with cash back offers of up to Rs 10,000.

Acer has launched its 2026 Predator Helios gaming laptop lineup in India, bringing Nvidia's latest RTX 50 Series GPUs and Intel's Arrow Lake processors to a market increasingly driven by gaming, content creation, and AI workloads.

Three Models, One Target: Performance

The company unveiled three machines at the Next@Acer India event in Delhi on August 10: the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI, Predator Helios Neo 16 AI, and the standard Predator Helios Neo 16.

The top-spec Predator Helios Neo 16 AI is powered by an Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX processor paired with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU with 16GB GDDR7 VRAM. It features a 16-inch WQXGA OLED display with a 240Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and full DCI-P3 color coverage. Storage and memory go up to 2TB PCIe Gen4 SSD and 64GB DDR5 RAM, respectively.

The slimmer Helios Neo 16S AI squeezes similar performance into a chassis under 18.9mm thick, pairing an Intel Core Ultra 7 356H processor with an RTX 5060 GPU and a 165Hz OLED display with VESA DisplayHDR True Black 1000 certification.

The entry-level Helios Neo 16 runs on Intel's previous-generation Core i9-14900HX with an RTX 5070 GPU, a 180Hz display, and up to 32GB DDR5 RAM — positioned for mainstream gamers who want current-gen graphics without the premium price tag.

"The new Predator Helios lineup represents our vision of delivering uncompromising performance across every gaming segment."

— Sudhir Goel, Chief Business Officer, Acer India

Pricing and Availability

The Predator Helios Neo 16 starts at Rs 2,42,990, the slim Neo 16S AI at Rs 2,62,990, and the flagship Neo 16 AI at Rs 2,82,990. All three come with cash back offers of up to Rs 10,000 and are available at Acer Exclusive Stores, the Acer E-store, Amazon, Flipkart, Croma, Reliance, and Vijay Sales.

Global availability had been uncertain heading into 2026, with the industry grappling with component shortages. RAM and SSDs have been in tight supply as AI infrastructure absorbs growing volumes of memory chips, driving up costs for consumer hardware. The Predator Helios lineup was initially announced at CES 2026 in January and reached international markets in mid-year.

Coders, Not Just Gamers

Acer India has noted a shift in its buyer profile. In an interview with The Indian Express, an Acer India executive said coders and developers are now a significant driver of GPU laptop demand, with EMI financing making machines that cost over Rs 2 lakh more accessible than they once were.

All three laptops integrate Acer Intelligence Space and PredatorSense, a software hub for system monitoring, AI-assisted features, and overclocking controls. The cooling systems use Acer's 5th-generation AeroBlade 3D fans, liquid metal thermal grease, and vector heat pipes to manage heat during sustained workloads.

What It Means for Buyers in India

The launch comes as Nvidia's Blackwell architecture and DLSS 4.5 bring meaningful performance jumps in both gaming and professional workflows. For buyers in India, the availability of RTX 5080-class hardware at launch pricing — rather than the inflated street prices seen with previous GPU generations — is a positive signal.

However, the starting prices remain firmly in premium territory. Buyers weighing these machines against competitors from Asus, MSI, and Lenovo will find a crowded field at this price point, where display quality, thermal performance, and after-sales service often matter as much as raw specifications.
nri_angle: Indian tech enthusiasts and NRIs considering laptop purchases in India can now access RTX 50 Series hardware at launch, a shift from the delayed availability typical of previous generations.
